hints: The existing list is already sorted and clean. Which bookings can the new one not affect at all — those that finish before it starts, or those that start after it ends?
One linear pass in three phases: copy intervals ending before extra starts, fuse every interval that overlaps/touches extra into it (stretch its start and end), then copy the rest.

1. Copy every booking whose end < extra start.
  2. While a booking's start ≤ extra end: set extra start = min, extra end = max.
  3. Add the stretched extra.
  4. Copy all remaining bookings.
  5. Return the list.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Append extra to the list, sort again and run the general merge.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Use the existing order: three-phase single scan (before, overlapping, after).

explain: In sample 1, extra = [5,9]. [1,2] ends before 5, so it is copied as is. [4,6] starts at 4 ≤ 9, so extra becomes [4,9]; [9,11] starts at 9 ≤ 9 (touching), so extra becomes [4,11]. Nothing remains, giving [[1,2],[4,11]]. Because the list is sorted and non-overlapping, all intervals that touch extra sit together in one run, so one pass is enough. Edge cases: an empty booked list, or extra landing before or after everything.
recognize: Insert one interval into an already sorted, non-overlapping list → linear scan: before / overlap / after.
